[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Seq2Seq Architecture and Encoder-Decoder Models in NLP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) architecture forms the backbone of modern Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks where both the input and output are variable-length sequences. Prominent applications include machine translation, text summarization, and conversational chatbots."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Components of Seq2Seq Models"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The standard Seq2Seq framework consists of two main neural network components: the Encoder and the Decoder, typically implemented using Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), LSTMs, or GRUs."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Encoder: Processes the input sequence token by token and compresses the semantic information into a fixed-size context vector (or hidden state)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Context Vector: The final hidden state of the encoder that encapsulates the entire meaning of the input sequence."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Decoder: Takes the context vector as its initial hidden state and generates the target output sequence step by step."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing a Basic Seq2Seq Encoder in PyTorch"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a practical implementation of a recurrent encoder using PyTorch to demonstrate how input sequences are mapped to hidden representations."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Encoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, emb_dim, hid_dim, n_layers):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(input_dim, emb_dim)
        self.rnn = nn.LSTM(emb_dim, hid_dim, n_layers, batch_first=True)
        
    def forward(self, src):
        embedded = self.embedding(src)
        outputs, (hidden, cell) = self.rnn(embedded)
        return hidden, cell"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing the Decoder"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The decoder takes the encoder's final hidden and cell states and generates the output tokens sequentially using teacher forcing during training."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"class Decoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, output_dim, emb_dim, hid_dim, n_layers):
        super().__init__()
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(output_dim, emb_dim)
        self.rnn = nn.LSTM(emb_dim, hid_dim, n_layers, batch_first=True)
        self.fc_out = nn.Linear(hid_dim, output_dim)
        
    def forward(self, input, hidden, cell):
        input = input.unsqueeze(1)
        embedded = self.embedding(input)
        output, (hidden, cell) = self.rnn(embedded, (hidden, cell))
        prediction = self.fc_out(output.squeeze(1))
        return prediction, hidden, cell"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Limitations of Basic Seq2Seq Models"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"While powerful, standard encoder-decoder models suffer from a fundamental bottleneck: forcing the entire input sentence into a single fixed-length context vector leads to information loss, especially for very long sequences. This limitation motivated the development of Attention Mechanisms."}]
